claims.text: Other hospitals registered in Varginha in the same national register include Hospital Bom Pastor (CNES 2761092, Fundação Hospitalar do Município de Varginha) and Hospital Unimed Varginha (CNES 2761319).

The identification of the 'Hospital Regional de Varginha' of the 1996 case narrative with the registered Hospital Regional do Sul de Minas is a reasoned match on name, city and the fact that it is the only regional hospital in the municipal register. Reasoning: no contemporaneous 1996 hospital document was obtained to confirm the identification.

No hospital admission, transfer or incident record from January 1996 was located in this pass; the custody sequence at this facility remains testimony-based and is a wave-4 target for Brazilian archival and municipal records requests.
Referenced by the board but no dossier written yet. This node exists so the graph resolves and so the gap is visible rather than silent — see the wave-3 queue.

connections.edgeLabel: Varginha discussed in a 2024 meeting with AARO staff
connections.label: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)
connections.note: Filmmaker James Fox says that in 2024 he met AARO personnel to discuss video his team had obtained and that the Varginha incident was among the cases debated, with AARO director Dr Jon Kosloski entering the room. This rests solely on Fox's account as reported by The Debrief; AARO's own 2024 report states no investigation has concluded that any UAP report indicates extraterrestrial origin, and the Pentagon did not respond to requests for comment.

connections.label: Anna Paulina Luna
connections.note: At a closed-door 15 January 2026 meeting in Rep. Tim Burchett's Longworth office, Dr Italo Venturelli, who says he was on duty at the Hospital Regional de Varginha in January 1996, described examining a non-human being at the hospital. Rep. Anna Paulina Luna, chair of the House Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets, questioned him directly and afterwards said Congress should seek Air Force flight records and landing authorisations to test the claimed US removal of the body. No medical record of the treatment exists, per Venturelli.

desc: The facility referred to in the Varginha literature as the Hospital Regional de Varginha is registered in Brazil's national health-establishment register, CNES, as the Hospital Regional do Sul de Minas, CNES code 2761041, at Rua Rui Barbosa 158, Centro, Varginha, Minas Gerais (CEP 37002-140), under municipal administration, operating continuous 24-hour service and providing SUS outpatient care. Varginha's other registered hospitals in the same register include the Hospital Bom Pastor, run by the municipal hospital foundation, and the Hospital Unimed Varginha. The hospital is on this board because it is one of the medical facilities named in the January 1996 Varginha case as a place to which an injured creature was reportedly taken and held before being moved on, in the sequence involving military and fire-brigade personnel that is recorded elsewhere on this board as ev-varginha-1996. The case is not a historical curiosity: it was carried to Capitol Hill on its thirtieth anniversary, and on 8 July 2026 a congressional demand went to the CIA and FBI for records on the Varginha and Campinas incidents - meaning that a municipal hospital in Minas Gerais is now a named location in an American records fight. What exists here as verified fact is the facility and its registry entry; the 1996 hospital-custody sequence rests on witness testimony and journalism, not on any hospital record obtained in this pass.
